findings.title: Global canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing view-only admins to create groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-arg, realm-wide check) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because the expected-scope list includes VIEW, an admin who was granted only the `view` scope on the type-level Groups resource passes `canManage()`/`requireManage()`. `requireManage()` guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups), so a view-only admin can create (and via the same check path move) top-level groups. This looks like a copy-paste from canView(); it should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, mirroring the per-group override at line 79 which correctly checks only MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs (UUIDs) instead of group IDs
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code does `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` and `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` where the resource *name* is the group ID; the resource *ID* is a store-generated UUID. The private hasPermission(String groupId, ...) at line 141 looks resources up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e. it expects a name, so passing a resource ID never finds the per-group resource and silently falls back to the type-level "Groups" resource. Worse, the returned set is consumed as *group IDs* by UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource (it is set as the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute used for storage-level filtering by group membership). An admin whose visibility comes from group member permissions therefore gets a set of resource UUIDs: the storage filter matches no groups, user searches return no users and user counts return 0 — notably for a type-level view-members/manage-members permission, where the UUID of the type-level resource is the only entry added. The V1 implementation this replaces explicitly derived group IDs from resource names (GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`). Additionally, getOrCreateResource never sets a resource type, so findByType("Groups") may only match the type-level resource and per-group view-members permissions may not be reflected in the set at all. The code should use groupResource.getName() for both the permission lookup and the granted set.

findings.title: V2 group permission management throws UnsupportedOperationException in code paths that are still invoked
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, etc.) to throw UnsupportedOperationException. But these methods are still called when the V2 feature is active: (1) AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:94) registers a GroupRemovedEvent listener whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled — which is the base feature the V2 feature builds on — and the listener calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. With MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returning GroupPermissionsV2, deleting any group fires the event and the listener throws, failing the group deletion (and if only V2 is enabled the listener is not registered, so per-group resources/policies are never cleaned up and stale authorization data accumulates). (2) GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled call permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group)/getPermissions(group), which previously worked (MgmtPermissionsV2 used the V1 GroupPermissions implementation) and now turn into HTTP 500 responses. These operations need real V2 implementations (e.g. resource/policy cleanup) rather than throwing.

findings.title: Tests leak created groups, making count assertions order-dependent
findings.body: In GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest, testManageAllGroups creates the group "testGroup" (later renamed to "newGroup") via ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse without registering a realm.cleanup() entry (compare the other tests that do `realm.cleanup().add(r -> r.groups().group(id).remove())`), and testManageGroup creates "subGroup" through the subGroup(...) call at line 226 (expecting 201) also without cleanup. The managed realm persists across test methods in the class, while testViewGroups asserts exact result sizes (hasSize(0), hasSize(1), hasSize(2)) and testManageAllGroups asserts exact counts of visible groups. Depending on JUnit's method execution order, the leaked groups make these assertions fail intermittently.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the newly added Groups resource type
findings.body: This PR adds the Groups resource type to the schema, but getResourceName() still only special-cases USERS: for a Users type-level resource it returns "All users" and maps per-user resources to the user's username. Group resources fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which for per-group resources created by getOrCreateResource is the raw group ID (the resource name). Permission/resource listings in the admin API and console will therefore show bare UUIDs for group permissions instead of a group name or path, unlike users.
